definitions: A candlestick pattern in technical analysis indicating a potential reversal of the current trend.
A two-candlestick pattern where a smaller candle is completely engulfed by the previous larger candle.
examples: Traders often look for a Harami pattern as a sign of trend exhaustion.
The appearance of a Harami pattern after a long uptrend can signal a bearish reversal.
Identifying a Harami pattern requires careful observation of candle sizes and positions.
